decisions.statement: The audit service keeps running rather than being started for each round.
A service stating a schedule is a one-shot unit a timer fires.
This service states none, so the hourly round is a loop of its own inside it.
A round opens as the service starts, and an hour after the round before.
A round judges its checks in the cluster rather than on this workstation.
What is newly refusing is worked out here, where the verdicts before it are.
A check the cluster left unjudged is unmeasured rather than run here.
A round the cluster would not take is said on the error stream.
A service always up has no round to catch up on.
A round that threw is said on the error stream and leaves the service listening.
A stop ends the service at once rather than waiting out the round underway.
A round runs far longer than the seconds a stop is given.
A check a stop ended part way has no verdict, so the round after runs it.
A round is asked for over HTTP rather than by starting the service.
The port is the one after the pages service's, those two being what listens here.
A round is asked for from this workstation, so the loopback is bound alone.
No caller of the audit service is asked for a credential.

definition: the service running each check's audit and telling whoever champions checks what turned red
